questions.question: Where should shipping papers for hazardous materials be placed?

options.text: At the bottom of the stack of shipping papers.
On top of the stack of shipping papers.
In a separate location from non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: On top of the stack of shipping papers.
questions.explanation: Drivers and carriers must find hazardous materials papers quickly. Hazardous materials shipping papers must be placed on top of the stack.

questions.question: What must you keep in the vehicle when transporting chlorine?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers saved

questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must keep an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in their vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if corrosive materials leak in the trailer?
questions.explanation: Vehicle parts that touch corrosive materials must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: Which location is NOT acceptable for keeping hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door
In a pouch on the passenger's side door
Within the driver's reach while wearing a seat belt
On the driver's seat when the driver is outside the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door
questions.explanation: When driving, hazardous materials papers must be in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view and reach of the driver. When the driver leaves the vehicle, papers should be on the driver's seat.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check tire pressure?
questions.explanation: You must use a tire gauge during the vehicle inspection test to check tire pressure. Simply kicking the tires will not pass the test.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, what is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs. On roads with multiple lanes, turn into the correct lane. Always use or stay in the rightmost lane unless the lane is blocked.

questions.question: What should you do during the stop/start maneuver on the skills test?

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to reach the shoulder.
Slam on the brakes to stop as fast as possible.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you will pull over and stop as if checking your vehicle. Check traffic, use your turn signal, slow down smoothly with steady braking and gear changes, and come to a full stop without coasting.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a minor truck fire?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: If you have a truck fire, feel the doors before opening them to see if they are hot. Hot doors may mean there is a cargo fire inside. Keep cargo doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: What must a person supervising tank loading do?

options.text: Does not need to be able to move the vehicle.
Does not need to know about the materials being loaded.
Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch tank loading and unloading. They must stay alert, see the tank clearly, stay within 25 feet of it, know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: What can result in points against your basic control skills test score?

options.text: Touching or crossing an exercise boundary line.
Getting out once to check your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Touching or crossing an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each time this happens counts as an error and costs points on your test score.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass, or change lanes. Keep your vehicle in the same lane until you have completely crossed the tracks.

questions.question: When entering an expressway, you should:

options.text: Abruptly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: Before entering an expressway, check the traffic carefully. Use your signals and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: If a shipping paper shows both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials can be identified by:

options.text: Non-hazardous materials being written in pencil.
Being written larger than non-hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be distinguished from non-hazardous materials in one of three ways: listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in the "HM" column.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must be shown?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging containing the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If the letter "G" (for "Generic") appears in Column 1, the technical name of the hazardous material must also be listed.

questions.question: Your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: Exactly where the examiner has instructed it to be.
Within five feet of the final position described by the examiner.
Within two feet of the final position described by the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner has instructed it to be.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle exactly where the examiner tells you. Failing to do this can result in failure of the driving test.

questions.question: Shippers must keep a copy of shipping papers for:
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep copies or images of shipping papers for at least two years after the materials are picked up by the carrier. For hazardous waste, the time period is three years.

questions.question: Hazardous materials laws are controlled by:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are regulated by federal, state, and local governments because of the risks involved in transporting them.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must show all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating range.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: Check that the oil pressure gauge works properly. The warning light should turn off or the gauge should show normal pressure. The oil temperature gauge should gradually rise to normal operating range. The oil pressure gauge should not be connected to the brakes.

questions.question: Portable tanks:

options.text: Cannot be removed from a vehicle.
Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
Are permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Portable tanks are not permanently attached to a vehicle. Cargo tanks stay attached to a vehicle at all times.

questions.question: Who must put placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The shipper provides the placards, but the driver is responsible for putting them on the vehicle.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts should be all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Lug nuts must be tight. They should have no cracks, distortions, or rust. Check that all bolt holes are also free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the left. Park completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: After driving under an overpass, what may you be asked to recall?

options.text: If there was a shoulder near the roadway.

questions.explanation: During the road test, the examiner may ask you to recall the height or clearance posted on an overpass you passed.

questions.question: A sign that a shipment contains hazardous materials is:

options.text: The shipper works in a business that typically handles hazardous materials, such as a fireworks dealer or pest control firm.
The last shipment you picked up was labeled as hazardous.
The shipper's business is located in a bad part of town.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper works in a business that typically handles hazardous materials, such as a fireworks dealer or pest control firm.
questions.explanation: Look at what type of business the shipper operates. If they deal in paint, chemicals, fireworks, or pest control, the shipment likely contains hazardous materials.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials include explosives, flammable gases, and flammable solids. Regular rocks are not hazardous materials.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if the engine must run to operate a pump.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves open while loading and unloading compressed gas. Close them when not loading or unloading.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking maneuvers.

questions.question: What should a carrier do if hazardous materials are not properly prepared?

options.text: Accept the shipment, but make a notation on the paperwork

questions.explanation: The carrier must refuse any shipment of hazardous materials that is not properly prepared.
